title: Zelensky: The Middle East War Is Draining Ukraine's Air Defense Missiles
dek: The US makes only 60 to 65 missiles a month, and 803 were used on the first day of the Middle East war. Zelensky says what Putin wants is a long war, because running down resources hurts Ukraine.
why: Medium information density, but Zelensky gives several concrete numbers and judgments, more substantive than a press release. The second half, a conversation about himself and his family, can be fast-forwarded.
who: Founders and investors watching geopolitics, the defense supply chain and the trajectory of the Russia-Ukraine war, especially those who want to understand how the Middle East war indirectly affects Europe's security order.
skip: The last five minutes on family and children, low information density, can be skipped.

points.h: The Middle East war directly drains Ukraine's air defense missiles
points.body: Zelensky says the Middle East war's impact on Ukraine is direct: a global fuel shortage and, more importantly, air defense missile supply being squeezed. He states plainly that "there will be a reduced number of missiles for our defense." He is already looking for alternatives, because Ukraine was short on anti-missile missiles this past winter, and the next winter will still come. He also says America's diplomatic focus is now on the Middle East, and trilateral talks keep getting postponed for one reason only: the Iran war.

points.h: What Putin wants is exactly a long war
points.body: Zelensky's judgment is that for Putin, a long war in Iran is a plus. The reason is not only energy prices, but that it consumes America's reserves and the production capacity of air defense missile manufacturers. When the US needs extra resources it turns to Europe, and Europe as an ally gives. The result is that resources do not flow to Ukraine. Zelensky says Putin needs to weaken Ukraine, and the Middle East is one of the ways to do that.

points.h: What the US makes in a month, the Middle East burns in a day
points.body: Zelensky gives a set of concrete numbers: the US produces 60 to 65 missiles a month, roughly 700 to 800 a year. The first day of the Middle East war used 803. He says Middle Eastern countries used PAC-3 to intercept drones early in the war, because PAC-3 can hit any aerial target. The question now is when Middle East stockpiles run out. His conclusion: Ukraine will definitely face a missile shortage.

points.h: What Ukraine wants is production licenses, not sympathy
points.body: Zelensky's demands of Western leaders are specific: unity first, speed second. He says Ukraine became first in military technology because of the war, not because it is smarter, but because it has underground manufacturers. What he wants is for European friends to give Ukraine's industrial sector the maximum licenses, rights and opportunities so Ukraine can produce the weapons it is short of itself. He says this is Ukraine's first interest.

points.h: Trump wants to end the war but does not want to pick a side
points.body: Zelensky says he believes Trump genuinely wants to end the war, because Trump promised voters and wants to finish quickly. But Trump's strategy is to keep close dialogue with Putin, not to provoke him, while not fully siding with Ukraine. Zelensky says Trump positions himself as a mediator, not on either side. Ukraine wants Trump on Ukraine's side, because the more countries stand with Ukraine, the more pressure on Russia. But America has its own strategy.

points.h: Putin is not prepared to sign any agreement, only to dictate an ultimatum
points.body: Zelensky says Putin is not prepared to sign any agreement; what he wants is for Ukraine to sign an ultimatum. Putin understands that giving up the Donbas means splitting Ukrainian society, and a split society can be exploited. Zelensky says Putin's goal is division, because a divided country is a weak country that can be occupied further. He says Ukraine is ready to compromise, especially if the US is involved, but the US has not demanded major compromises from Russia.

points.h: The Russian regime should be treated as fairly as Iran
points.body: Zelensky says the West must be fair toward different regimes. If there is a certain attitude toward Maduro or the Iranian regime, the same attitude should apply to the Russian regime, because they are no different on human rights, freedom or nuclear threats. He says the first step should be a diplomatic solution, but in a tough way, giving Putin the same terms as other regimes. He states plainly that toppling the regime is the second step; the first step is diplomacy.

points.h: If Ukraine enters NATO, the war is over
points.body: Zelensky reiterates that he is willing to give up his position if it can be exchanged for NATO membership. He says if NATO recognizes Ukraine's army as one of Europe's strongest, he is willing to consider that he has done everything. He says if Ukraine is in NATO, the war is over. He also says he does not think there is a big problem in the relationship between Trump and Starmer, and that history is stronger than the emotions of two or three people.
